decisions.reason: A catalog display variant made on existing corrugated equipment costs little to keep listed, and with no evidence since 2019 its value is still uncertain, so the option stays open.
The pegboard shelf display fits the core display portfolio and is cheap to maintain, and nothing so far shows its value will not be realized.
The quarter-pallet shelf display is a standard format with steady retail demand and very low holding cost, so keeping it is justified.
The eighth-pallet format meets the trend toward smaller promotional displays, and keeping it open costs little while uncertainty remains.
The wooden pallet lies outside the paper core and likely needs outside sourcing, which raises its holding cost, but without negative evidence the option is still kept for now.
Demand for physical media retail displays is structurally declining, so this is the weakest option, yet the low marginal cost of a catalog variant still narrowly favors keeping it.
